715200101.text: There's no way I'm gonna finish this... Guess I have no choice but to reduce the scale of my experiment. Let me think... How should I explain this to my mentor?

715200102.text: "Ohh, my experiment is way too hard to conduct! It's impossible to find the right materials, and I still failed after trying everything I could to build an ideal experiment environment!"

715200103.text: Ugh, what a lame excuse... I'm sure my mentor won't have any of that...

715200104.text: Maybe you should just tell him up front that you can't complete this project, then come up with a new proposal!

715200105.text: Wh—Whoa... Don't just join the conversation when someone's talking to themselves!

715200106.text: Oh hey, it's you! Do you still remember me? I'm Jami, an Amurta researcher.

715200108.text: Yep, that's me. The Amurta researcher who was tormented by his thesis proposal and was this close to seeing the Dendro Archon.

715200111.text: *sigh* Anyway, thank you for that suggestion, but as things currently stand, I'm pretty much past the point of no return... If I discontinue this project, my mentor would no doubt skin me alive...

715200112.text: And that won't be all. He'll leave me to dry and turn me into a specimen, then place me inside the Amurta labs. My label would say "Jami, who failed to live up to his mentor's expectations."

715200113.text: Sounds like the start of another urban legend at the Akademiya... Would mentors really do that?

715200115.text: Heh, I guess becoming a specimen wouldn't be too bad... I can at least serve as a warning to my juniors...

715200117.text: But why can't you just stop? You shouldn't force yourself to do something you can't do.

715200118.text: It's complicated... and it's not really impossible to do either. I conducted a similar experiment in the past and even obtained some workable data...

715200119.text: Oh, that's great! Just continue working on your experiment then!

715200120.text: *sigh* But everything went downhill from there. My previous experiment was such a huge success that my Darshan began having high hopes for my project. Even my mentor gave me a few compliments.

715200121.text: "You can do it Jami, I believe in you!" ...Who would've thought that cranky old man would say something like that?

715200110.text: I'm that researcher whose proposal got rejected twice and couldn't get started on his experiment... They called me the "groaning Akademiya researcher" Jami.
